verified_scope: Exact native reception of raw auxiliary high nibbles, and their measured effect on drum onsets and melodic note length; predictions that failed are kept as failed

predictions.reception: The backup equals the compiled target exactly (every packet and the whole body), raw auxiliary bytes included

H1_drum_retrigger.statement: A drum step with high nibble n in 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 plays n onsets within its own step (the retrigger counts the device's interface cycles through)

H0_drum_no_effect.statement: The nibble has no audible effect on a drum step: every probe plays one onset in its step, as stray-bits-results.md would suggest

H1_melodic_length.statement: A melodic note with high nibble n in 1, 2, 4, 8 sounds for n steps (250 ms each, within 60 ms); F and E sound the whole 3 s tone, being longer than it

H0_melodic_no_effect.statement: The nibble has no audible effect on a melodic note: every probe sounds the whole 3 s tone (within 100 ms), as stray-bits-results.md found for nibbles 2 and E

session_answers.question: Patterns 1 to 4 (clicks): did some steps play a quick burst of repeated clicks rather than one? Roughly how many? (notes)
Patterns 5 to 10 (a steady tone, one per bar): did some tones stop short of the others? (notes)
Did the device show ERR, or anything unusual on its screen? (yes/no/notes)

limits: Onset counting assumes repeats are separated by at least 12 ms; a retrigger faster than that would be undercounted
A length unit other than one step would fail H1 and show in the measured durations
